evals.prompt: On this org NixOS client, use our deployed remote builder to compile something and prove it really compiled remotely rather than coming from a cache or an existing local output. The hello package may already have been built here. Do not edit a repo or deploy anything. Save the exact commands, relevant log evidence, and a short conclusion.
evals.expected_output: A successful root store connectivity check and a fresh no-substitutes build with local jobs disabled, with explicit log evidence naming euc-hel-0 and no reliance on --rebuild.
expectations: Checks the root nix-daemon connection with sudo nix store info --store ssh-ng://euc-hel-0
Uses a genuinely fresh derivation or otherwise proves the output was not already present
Disables local jobs with --max-jobs 0 and disables substituters for the proof
Provides actual build-log evidence naming ssh-ng://nix-ssh@euc-hel-0
Does not rely on the incompatible --rebuild plus zero-local-jobs combination and does not edit or deploy configuration

evals.prompt: A package is misbehaving only when it builds on our remote builder. Give me a one-off command to build .#packages.x86_64-linux.example entirely locally, without permanently disabling the remote builder. Also explain the normal way to offload this repo's NixOS VM tests and why a build might legitimately stay local even when the builder is healthy.
evals.expected_output: A per-invocation empty builders override, normal scheduler and VM feature guidance, and no persistent configuration change or confusion with max-jobs 0.
expectations: Uses --builders '' or an equivalent per-command empty builders setting to force local compilation
States that the override is temporary and does not edit persistent Nix configuration
Does not recommend --max-jobs 0 for forcing a local build
Mentions euc-hel-0's kvm and nixos-test features and use of the repo's normal VM-test runner or test derivation
Explains that Nix may schedule locally despite a healthy builder because speedFactor is a preference rather than mandatory remote placement

evals.prompt: After euc-hel-0 was reinstalled, my client's nix-daemon logs say Host key verification failed. Show me a safe debugging path that does not weaken SSH host-key checking or expose keys. I also changed the remote-builder clanService's supportedFeatures and SSH timeout; which exact tests should I run before asking a human to deploy?
evals.expected_output: Root/daemon diagnostics, source-and-vars based host-key repair without bypasses, the focused nix-unit check and full clanServices and home checks, and no agent deploy.
expectations: Includes -L build output, /etc/nix/machines, root store info, and nix-daemon journal diagnostics without printing private keys
Attributes the likely host-key failure to stale pinned trust after reinstall and requires verifying current public key material and source generations
Explicitly avoids disabling host-key checking, deleting the mismatch as a fix, or recommending unsupported nix log over ssh-ng
Runs or prescribes nix fmt, nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.nix-unit -L, and nix flake check --show-trace in clanServices
Checks home inventory integration and leaves vars generation and deployment to a human in the correct server-before-new-client order
